dispose

/dih-SPOHZ/ — rhymes with "rose" · verb

Hear It

What It Means

To dispose of something is to throw it away or get rid of it for good.

Please dispose of the batteries at the recycling center, not in the trash.

Example

After the art project ended, the teacher helped students dispose of the toxic paint cans at the hazardous waste facility, ensuring they would never harm the environment.

Dispose means more than just throwing away — it emphasizes responsible, proper removal. The word carries the sense of handling something in a careful, lawful way, which is exactly why the hazardous waste facility is mentioned rather than a regular trash bin.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

junk: To junk something is to toss it out casually because it seems worthless — no ceremony, no procedure. To dispose of something points the other way: a careful, proper, often official process of removal. You junk a frayed phone charger; a hospital disposes of used equipment by the rules.

trash: To trash something is to throw it into the ordinary garbage. Dispose covers the removals a garbage can is not allowed to handle — the word signals a responsible, often lawful process, with rules about where a thing must go. Motor oil is never trashed; it is handled properly.

scrap: To scrap something is to get rid of it because it no longer works or will never be finished — a rusted car, a failed plan. Dispose is about the manner of removal, careful and proper, while scrap is about the verdict that a thing is past saving.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

retain: to continue to keep possession of

preserve: to keep something safe from harm

Where it sits · how deliberate and final the removal — toss → throw away → dispose → eliminate

toss vs. dispose: Toss is much more casual than dispose — you toss a wrapper without a second thought, while to dispose of something is to get rid of it deliberately and for good.

throw away vs. dispose: Throw away is weaker than dispose; throwing something away is the everyday act of putting it in the trash, while disposing of it suggests a careful, final, proper method of removal.

eliminate vs. dispose: Eliminate is stronger than dispose — disposing of something gets rid of it properly, but eliminating it wipes it out completely, leaving no trace at all.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart, away (Latin)

Root — pose

Root — pose: to put, place (from pōnere, via French poser) (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Dis- ('away') plus pose ('to put, place') builds the idea of putting something away from you for good — which is exactly what you do when you dispose of trash properly.

Use the root in a new word: deposit

Use the root in a new word: deposit: She stopped at the bank on Friday afternoon to deposit her first paycheck.

Word Choice

formal / neutral

Dispose suggests a formal, responsible, and often lawful process — especially for waste, hazardous materials, or official handling. For everyday throwing away, "throw away" is simpler and more natural.
